docRequirement: env-vars.md:280, the `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` row, read whole: "Number of [subagent layers](/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents) allowed below the main conversation (default: 3). At the default, subagents can spawn their own subagents, and a subagent at the third layer can't spawn further; set `1` to turn nesting off. In v2.1.217 through v2.1.218, the default was 1, so a subagent couldn't spawn its own unless you raised the limit; v2.1.219 raised the default to 3. Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed." Three bindings: (a) the DEFAULT ceiling is three subagent layers below the main conversation; (b) an environment variable named `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` adjusts that ceiling, with `1` as the documented "nesting off" value; (c) the reader's parse contract is strict — a positive whole number in PLAIN DIGITS only (the sibling `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION` row at :279 spells out that the family "doesn't take the scientific notation or digit-separator spellings"), anything else is IGNORED and falls back to the default, and there is no value that removes the limit — so `0` must not mean unlimited.

divergence: Two deltas on one knob, and neither is a naming problem — the field names, the wire shape and the enforcement point are all right. (1) VALUE: our default and effective ceiling is 1 where env-vars.md:280 says 3, i.e. we ship the page's documented "set `1` to turn nesting off" configuration as the unconditional product behaviour. This was correct parity for v2.1.217-2.1.218 and was chosen for that reason; v2.1.219 moved the page to 3 and our value did not move. (2) READER ABSENT: the variable itself has no counterpart at all — there is no `NESSY_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`, no compat read of `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`, and the `orchestrator.depth` key that would carry it is never populated by host code, so the limit is fixed rather than defaulted. Putting the variable in a settings `env` block — the exact remedy the page prescribes — does nothing. This half is a genuine absence inside an otherwise working mechanism, which is why the finding is `built-wrong` rather than `not-built`: nothing needs inventing, one number moves and one reader is added. The parse contract of that reader is the part this page (rather than sub-agents.md) pins down: plain digits only, malformed ignored, no disable value — so `0` must fall back to 3 and must not be read as unlimited, and the repo's nearest existing numeric reader (`mcpAutoBackgroundDelayMs`, `background-task-settings.ts:118-122`) uses bare `Number(raw)` and would wrongly accept `1e3`/`0x10`, so the `print-background-wait.ts` `/^\d+$/` shape is the one to copy.

userImpact: Observable today, and it presents as a hard product limitation rather than a setting. A subagent cannot delegate at all: the ceiling is one layer below the main conversation and there is no way for a user to lift it. Two surfaces. (1) The common case is silent — an agent (the user's own or one imported from a Claude/Codex plugin) that declares no `tools` list never receives `subagent` at all (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:141`), so a reviewer agent asked to "dispatch a verifier per finding" quietly does the whole job itself in one context: the user sees a flatter, slower, more context-hungry run and no message explaining why. (2) The explicit case is a visible mid-run tool error — an author who lists `subagent`/`Agent` in the agent's `tools` gets `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` back from the first delegation, in the subagent's transcript. In both cases the documented remedy does not work: setting `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (or any Nessy spelling) in the environment or a settings `env` block has no effect, because nothing reads it — a user porting a Claude Code setup that relies on a two- or three-layer agent tree gets a silently flattened run with no diagnostic and no knob.
